absent: Locking discipline for early setup, allocator reservation and resource insertion is not visible in these fragments.
Complete layouts of boot header, chained payload, measurement descriptor, handover descriptor and indirect descriptor beyond observed fields.
Behavior of delegated helpers for memory tables, firmware tables, device tree, entropy pool, hypervisor, timers, interrupts and topology.
Exact numeric values of setup kinds, resource flags, page sizes and error codes beyond names observed.
Failure handling beyond warnings for mapping errors and reservation conflicts.
Concurrency, reentrancy and ordering guarantees across bring up phases beyond the observed call sequence.

findings.text: Main early x86 initialization entry invoked once during boot with a place to publish the final command line; it orchestrates trap setup, parameter parsing, memory discovery and reservation, mapping activation, firmware and topology discovery, and timer and unwind preparation before handing control onward.

Public init time helpers expose the preserved measurement area: one releases the reservation and clears tracking state, another validates the tracked range and returns a kernel mapping plus length; both report absence when no area is tracked.
Public init time routine claims the fixed legacy personal computer port ranges for exclusive kernel use by registering each descriptor against the global port pool.
Public configuration helper synchronizes the supported page protection mask with processor execute disable capability, enabling the no execute bit when present and removing it otherwise.

Boot payload walk starts from the header link and follows successor addresses to termination, interpreting each item by numeric kind and delegating to memory table extension, device tree, firmware interface, measurement, handover, or randomness handling, ignoring unknown kinds.

Reservation walk traverses the same header linked chain and protects each header plus payload in the early allocator, with special handling that also protects the target of indirect entries unless nested, tolerating mapping failures by warning and stopping.

Overall bring up orders early traps and processor and mapping preparation before parameter parsing and reservations, completes firmware memory discovery before allocator activation and full mapping, then proceeds to firmware tables, interrupts, topology and timers, with crash reservation deferred until hot plug information is available.

Early measurement handling maps only a fixed size descriptor after the generic header, reserves the described physical span when length is nonzero and records its address and size globally, warning and doing nothing when mapping fails or the feature is disabled.

Handover handling is skipped with a warning when the handover feature is disabled; otherwise it maps the variable length payload after the generic header and forwards the embedded firmware table and scratch addresses and sizes to the handover population step before unmapping.

Boot header consumption decodes root device, display and loader identity with extended type expansion, derives loader version, records ram disk start when enabled, detects firmware boot flavour from loader signature, and adjusts default mount writability when root flags are clear.

Crash reservation stays inactive unless the reservation feature is enabled and command line parsing succeeds, is skipped on Xen paravirtual domains with an informational message, and otherwise delegates to generic and contiguous memory reservation helpers.

Kernel image segments for executable code, read only data, writable data and zero initialized data are published as memory resources derived from linker boundaries and inserted into the global memory pool; if the image span is not fully classified as usable ram, a warning is emitted and the firmware table is adjusted to force that span to usable ram.

Early reservation protects the kernel image up to a defined end marker and protects low sixty four KiB including page zero, then reserves setup payloads, firmware regions and model specific pages; firmware table sanitization marks the first page reserved and removes the conventional firmware window from usable ram; both initrd reservation helpers in this variant perform no action.

Sandy Bridge graphics workaround activates only when peripheral access is allowed and the graphics device at bus zero slot two function zero matches a known vendor and one of seven device identifiers; when active it reserves a small set of single pages known to be inaccessible, warning on failure.

Panic time offset reporting distinguishes randomized versus disabled layout, announcing base, relocation bounds and module ceiling when active. Protection reporting announces missing capability, active protection on sixty four bit or physical address extension builds, or inability to enable on legacy thirty two bit builds.
Bootloader randomness entries are consumed once into the entropy pool and then both payload and length are explicitly cleared so accidental re entry cannot reuse the seed, preserving forward secrecy.

Chained boot payload items share a common header carrying payload length, numeric kind and physical successor link plus variable payload bytes; indirect items embed an inner descriptor with its own kind, address and length.
Resource descriptors pair a readable name with inclusive start and end addresses and flag bits indicating busy state and address space kind, used for both port ranges and memory segments.
Measurement payloads carry a target physical address and length; handover payloads carry firmware table address and size plus scratch address and size.

Legacy port map facts use inclusive bounds: first DMA 0x00 to 0x1f, first interrupt controller 0x20 to 0x21, timer zero 0x40 to 0x43, timer one 0x50 to 0x53, keyboard data 0x60 alone and command 0x64 alone, DMA page 0x80 to 0x8f, second interrupt controller 0xa0 to 0xa1, second DMA 0xc0 to 0xdf, floating point 0xf0 to 0xff.

Sandy Bridge workaround facts: vendor 0x8086 at bus zero device two; device identifiers 0x0102 0x0112 0x0122 0x0106 0x0116 0x0126 0x010a; inaccessible pages at 0x20050000 0x20110000 0x20130000 0x20138000 0x40004000 each one page.
Low memory facts: first 4 KiB is firmware owned, first 64 KiB reserved for corruption and side channel safety, conventional firmware window from 640 KiB to 1 MiB excluded from usable ram.

Early temporary mappings can fail; each consumer warns and abandons only the affected item or chain rather than proceeding with invalid pointers. Unreserved low memory risks firmware corruption and disclosure, misclassified kernel ranges risk crashes, and specific graphics pages risk device inaccessibility if not excluded.
